The petitioner filed this petition against the respondent U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 for claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is that, on 27/11/2022 at about 11.30 a.m. while the minor petitioner was travelling as a passenger in KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-1308 Near Channapura Gate, Bangalore to Kolar NH-75 Road, Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, the driver of the Bus was driving the same in a rash and negligent manner and ran over the divider and after turtle the bus and caused the accident.
Due to that impact the petitioner and other passengers were sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Ashwini Super Speciality Hospital and admitted as an inpatient, the duty doctors examined her clinically and radiologically, which revealed that she sustained Left Shoulder shows epiphyseal injury with shaft of humerus fracture.
Accordingly, the petitioner is still under treatment and she was forced to spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges.

Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, she is completely bed ridden and undergoing deep mental shock,
pain and suffering, since the injuries caused permanent in nature and she is unable to do his work till the end of her life.

4. Prior to the date of accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 11 years, she was a student in private school, due to the said injuries, she is not able to do her daily activities.
Due to the accident, the petitioner is suffering from deep mental shock, pain and suffering, since the injuries caused permanent in nature.
It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-1308.
Hence, the respondent KSRTC being the owner of the offending Bus is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

5. In pursuance to the notice, the respondent appeared through its counsel & filed its objection and has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It is further contended that, the said offending bus was assigned on the schedule route from Bengaluru to Kolar and it was proceeding near Chennapura Gate on Chennai National Highway in moderate speed, it was dragged beyond the control, immediately the driver of the said bus applied the break and tried to avoid the possible hitting of the bus on either side of the road, but it was dragged beyond the control and went off the road by hitting the road side divider and then it was stopped.
Hence, there is no any negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus.

There is no any default of the KSRTC Bus and there is no rash and negligent act of the KSRTC Bus driver, the said driver is expert driver over the KSRTC Buses and have a speed lock system and hence, driving in high speed does not arise at all.

The petitioner know all these things and as such the petitioner is with active collusion with the police have implants the KSRTC Bus in an automobile Akanksha B.N vs K.S.R.T.C on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84014462/
2 accident
by converting the history of sell fall and false case filed by him and as such the claim petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

It has further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant and has also denied the age,
income and other averments made in the petition.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.
6. Based on the pleadings, following issues are framed:-

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 27-11- 2022 at about 11.30 A.M. when the petitioner was travelling as a passenger in KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-1308, near Channapura Gate, Bangalore-Kolar NH-75 road, Hosakote Taluk,
Bangalore Rural District, the driver of the said bus drive in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering human life, without following traffic rules, at a high speed and dashed to divider and jumped the divider after turtle the bus.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner and other passengers were fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3) What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, the guardian of the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got examined the Doctor by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.1 to P.17 documents.
On the other hand, the respondent got examined its Driver by name Sri. B. Mohan as RW.1 and got marked 04 documents as Ex.R.1 to R.4.
8. Heard the arguments.

9. My findings on the above issues as under:-
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ... In the Partly Affirmative, Issue No.3 ...
As per final Order, For the following:
REASONS 10. POINT No.1: The petitioner filed this petition against the respondent for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident, that occurred on 27/11/2022.
11.

In order to prove the case, the guardian of the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of petition in her chief examination affidavit and got marked 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12 documents.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of FIR, Ex.P.2 is the copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the copy of IMV report, Ex.P.5 is the copy of wound certificate,

.P.11 and 12 are the copy of Aadhar Cards.
Ex.P.15 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.16 is the medical bills and Ex.P.17 is the medical prescriptions.
In cross-examination, she has denied that, her minor daughter was not travelling in the said bus and there is no negligent driving by the bus driver.

12. The petitioner got examined the Dr. Nagaraj B.N. who is an Orthopaedic Surgeon, SOADS at Bangalore as PW.2 and he got marked 02 documents at Ex.P.13 and P.14, which are the X-ray and Clinical Examination Notes.

13. To disprove the case, respondent has examined its driver by name Sri. B. Mohan as RW.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 4 documents, which are Ex.R.1 is the copy of amount paid receipt, Ex.R.2 is the copy of cheque, Ex.R.3 is the copy of Discharge Summary and Ex.R.4 is the copy of Final Bill.
He has stated that, he was driving the vehicle by following all traffic rules in moderate speed.
The bus dragged beyond his control and went of the road and by hitting the divider got stopped.
In the cross-examination, he denied that the accident was caused due to his negligence.

14. On perusal of the evidence of PW.1 and Ex.P.3 spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 IMV Report, Ex.P.6 Charge Sheet, Ex.P.7 and 8 notice and reply to the notice, it appears that, the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-1308 drove the same at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
without observing traffic norms, so as to endangering human life near Chennapura Gate, on Bangalore-Kolar NH-75 Road, towards Kolar and lost control over the bus dashed to the divider of the Road, gone towards other side of the road and fell into a ditch and accident occurred.
Due to that tremendous impact the petitioner sustained injuries.
Hence, the Hosakote Police have registered the charge sheet against driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC and Sec.184 of IMV Act.

15. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the Petitioners have to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.

Hence, this Tribunal answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner claimed the compensation amount of Rs.10,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

The petitioner produced wound certificates and discharge summaries issued by MVJ Hospital, Hosakote, Bangalore Rural and Sri. Gaurav Orthopaedic & Surgical Hospital, Kolar and prayed to award compensation amount.
The respondents not disputed the said documents.
On perusal of the Ex.P.5 Wound Certificate it is discloses that, the petitioner has sustained the left shoulder shows that epiphyseal injury with shaft of humerous fracture.
The doctor opined that the injury is grievous in nature.

Therefore, taking all Akanksha B.N vs K.S.R.T.C on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84014462/
4

these facts and nature of injuries, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.20,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
18. The petitioner had produced medical bills and prescriptions, which are marked as Ex.P.9 and 16.
The respondents not denied the medical bills.

On perusal of the said medical bills and also considering the bills and also treatment taken by the petitioner in the hospitals, the petitioner is entitled to claim the medical bills amount of Rs.40,578/- under the head of medical expenditure.
19. As per Ex.P.15 discharge summary

, the petitioner took treatment at Sri. Gaurav Orthopaedic &
Surgical Hospital, Kolar from 13-06-2025 to 15-06-2025 for 03 days.

Therefore, by considering the period of treatment taken as inpatient this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.3,000/-
under the head Transportation, food, Nourishment and conveyance charges.

20. The guardian of the minor petitioner contended that, due to injuries the petitioner was suffering from pain and mental agony and she is unable to carry on his day to day activities which she used to do prior to the accident.
To prove the assessment of disability, the petitioner got examined one Doctor Shri. Nagaraj B.N. as PW-2.

In the chief examination affidavit PW.2 deposed that, on 02-05- 2025 the petitioner came to him for assessment of disability purpose and on examination the petitioner has healed scar over the left elbow, restricted left elbow movements with wasting of the left forearm muscles and the recent X-ray of the left humerus shows united fracture with implant-in-situ.
Further assessed the total physical disability of the Arm at 35% and the whole body disability of the petitioner at 12%.

In the cross-examination admitted that, personally he had not treated the petitioner and further admitted that, the fracture is united with implants in situ and there is no complication at the fractures site.
Further admitted that the shoulder and wrist movements of the petitioner are normal and there is loss of 10% movement at the elbow.
However by considering the nature of the wound, condition of the petitioner and evidence of the doctor this Tribunal has considered the disability of the Petitioner at 12% to the whole body.
21. The Petitioner was aged about 11 years at the time of accident.

In the case of minor injury the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, held in the case of Master Mallikarjun V/s Divisional Manager National Ins. Co. ltd., wherein it is held as under:
12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Rs.1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick.
In the instant case, the disability is to the tune of 18%.

Appellant had a longer period of hospitalization for about two months causing also inconvenience and loss of earning to the Akanksha B.N vs K.S.R.T.C on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84014462/
5 parents.
Herein this case the doctor assessed the disability caused to the arm of the Petitioner at 35% and that of to her whole body @ 12%.
It is pertinent note here that, the petitioner is a minor girl child and the dis-figuration of her hand would affect her future life and also would be hurdle for marriage.

Therefore, by considering the nature of the injury of the minor petitioner, age of the petitioner,
evidence of the doctor and period of treatment taken as an inpatient in the hospital, this Tribunal took the disability of the Petitioner at 12% to the whole body.
Hence, as per above cited citation the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- on account of the permanent disability.
22. The petitioner also sought for expenses towards future medicine for further treatment.
In the chief examination affidavit the doctor deposed that, she will require further surgeries for removal of implants and the approximate cost for the same is around Rs.60,000/-.
But, after examination of the PW.2, the evidence of PW.1 was reopened and further chief of PW.1 was recorded and Ex.P.15 to 17 are produced.

On perusal of Ex.P.15 the discharge summary it appears that the petitioner underwent surgery for implant removal and implants were removed and as per Ex.P.16 the bills were produced, which are considered in the coloumn of medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any future medical expenses.
23. The Petitioner sustained grievous injuries and also took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
The Petitioner also produced discharge summary and medical bills.
Therefore considering the nature of injury this Tribunal has award the amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities.

24. Considering the oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:

 permanent disability  4. Towards medical expenses Rs. 40,578/-

Towards future medical expenses Rs. NIL  6. Towards loss of amenities of life Rs. 30,000/-

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,93,578/-.

RW.1 has contended that, the respondent has paid the medical expenses of Rs.1,30,846/-
through the cheque.
On perusal of Ex.R.1 the copy of the payment receipt and Ex.R.2 the copy of the cheque, it appears that Rs.1,30,846/- is already paid to the petitioner.
Therefore, the said amount has to be deducted from the total compensation amount.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.2,62,732/-.
25. Interest:

In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
and not more than that.

entities.text: Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this Tribunal hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6%p.a. from the date of petition till the date of payment.
26. Liability:-
As per the petition, the respondent is the owner of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-1308.
As already discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Hence the respondent is liable to pay compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
27. Issue No.3

: For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.2,62,732/- interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Further, the Respondent is directed to deposit the compensation together with interest @6% p.a.
within 30 days, from the date of this order.
After deposit, Rs.1,12,732/- of compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the guardian of the minor petitioner with proper identification.
Remaining compensation amount of Rs.1,50,000/- with interest shall be deposit in FD in any nationalized bank in the name of the minor petitioner, till she attains the age of majority.
